text: The reticence of Genesis 22 is deliberate. The writer has set down within one narrative the God who promises and the God who demands; he leaves the opposition between them unresolved, and he declines, with a steadiness that is itself a kind of statement, to choose the one and dismiss the other. The question so raised is in its nature unanswerable. The reader, having followed Abraham up the mountain, is left where Abraham stands, with the knife lifted in his hand, and with no ram yet seen in the thicket.
